plans.free: WunderUI Free: the components with tier "free" are open source under the MIT License (https://github.com/wunder-ui/wunderui) — any project, commercial included. Every "pro" component needs WunderUI Core or Pro.
plans.core: WunderUI Core: every component, commercial license.
plans.pro: WunderUI Pro: everything in Core plus UI block and template source and all agent skills.

install.note: The npm package is WunderUI Free (the free components). Core and Pro install the full library from wunderui-core.

components.title: Accordion
components.description: Show one section at a time, or several, and keep long pages scannable.

props.name: disabled

keyboard: Tab: move between the headers
Enter / Space: open or close the focused panel
aria: Each trigger is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; each panel is labelled by its trigger
a11y.notes: hiddenUntilFound lets the browser's page search find and open closed panels.

parts.name: Accordion
parts.description: Holds which items are open. Opening one item closes the open one unless you set `multiple`. It takes an `appearance` of `plain`, `divided`, `contained` or `separated`, and a `density` of `default` or `compact`.

parts.name: AccordionItem
parts.description: One section. It draws the divider, the card or the hover fill, depending on the appearance of the list.

parts.name: AccordionTrigger
parts.description: The header row, a native `<button>` with `aria-expanded` inside a heading. It takes an optional leading `icon`, a `description` second line, a `meta` slot and an indicator.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The children of the trigger: the question or the section name. It is the accessible name of the button.

parts.name: Meta
parts.description: The `meta` slot between the label and the indicator, for a counter, a status or a short value.

parts.name: Indicator
parts.description: The chevron, plus or +/− that shows the open state. Set it with `indicatorVariant` and `indicatorPosition`; the default follows the appearance.

parts.name: AccordionContent
parts.description: The panel under the trigger. It opens on a grid-row transition, and its text lines up with the label.

parts.name: AccordionRow
parts.description: Wraps the trigger to put a control beside it, never inside it: `leading` (checkbox, switch) and `action` (a button such as Edit).

parts.name: AccordionFeedback
parts.description: The loading, empty and error content of a panel, with an optional action such as Retry.

items.text: Pick one `appearance` per list: `divided` or `plain` on a page, `contained` as one card, `separated` for stand-alone sections.
Use `density="compact"` (36 px rows) in side panels and `default` (48 px rows) everywhere else.
Set `multiple` on `Accordion` when people compare answers. By default, opening one item closes the one that was open.
Write the trigger as the question or the section name in sentence case: `How do refunds work?`. It is the button's accessible name.
Put controls beside the trigger with `AccordionRow`. The row keeps the trigger a single button and the control a separate stop for the keyboard.
Don't put buttons or links inside `AccordionTrigger`. The whole row is already a `<button>`, and a button inside a button is invalid HTML.
Don't hide what people must read or do in a closed row. Required information and primary actions belong outside the accordion.

components.description: A user or entity's profile image with a text fallback.

props.name: render

props.name: style

props.description: Whether the image element stays mounted and loads in place instead of being preloaded. Supports `loading="lazy"` and optimized image components such as `next/image`.

props.name: onLoadingStatusChange
props.description: Callback fired when the loading status changes.

parts.name: Avatar
parts.description: The round or square frame, in five sizes from `sm` to `xl`. Set `color` for tinted initials or `variant="primary"` for a filled one. With `interactive` it becomes a button with a hover and pressed halo and a focus ring; `selected` adds a check badge and `disabled` dims it.

parts.name: AvatarImage
parts.description: The photo, an `img` that takes `src` and `alt`. It shows once it has loaded; until then, or when the URL fails, the fallback stays in its place.

parts.name: AvatarFallback
parts.description: Initials or an icon, shown while the image loads or when there is none. The text size follows the avatar size.

parts.name: AvatarBadge
parts.description: A dot on the top right corner, centred on the edge of a circle or on the corner of a square. Set `status` for a presence dot whose shape differs per status and whose accessible name defaults to the status.

items.text: Use an Avatar to show who a person or workspace is, next to their name. For several people in little space, use Avatar Group or Avatar Stack.
Always add an `AvatarFallback` with initials, also when there is an image. It covers the moment before the photo loads and a broken image URL.
Use a circle for a person and a square for an entity such as a workspace, team or project, so the shape already tells which one it is.
Keep one `color` per person. The tints are theme tokens, so the initials stay readable in dark mode.
Show presence with `AvatarBadge` and say it in text where it matters, such as `Away` next to the name. Each status has its own shape, so colour is never the only signal.
Give an `interactive` avatar an accessible name with `aria-label`, for example `Account menu, Nora Lindgren`. Its initials are not a name.
Don't resize an avatar with classes like `size-12`. Pick `size` (`sm`, `xs`, `default`, `lg`, `xl`): initials, icon and presence dot scale with it.
Don't use `color` to carry status or meaning. Tone is an identity colour; status needs the presence dot, a word, or both.
Don't combine `selected` with a presence dot. The check badge and the dot sit on the same corner, so one hides the other.

components.title: Avatar Group
components.description: A stack of overlapping avatars, with an optional overflow count.

parts.name: AvatarGroup
parts.description: The row. It overlaps its avatars and rings each one in the surface colour, or spaces them with a 6 px gap. Hovering one lifts it and nudges its neighbours, except with reduced motion.

parts.name: Avatar
parts.description: Each person, an Avatar with initials or an image. Give all avatars in one group the same `size`.

parts.name: AvatarGroupCount
parts.description: The `+N` circle at the end for everyone not shown, a static count or a button. It takes the size of the avatars in the group.

items.text: Use an Avatar Group to show who is on a project or document, composing each avatar yourself. For people passed as data with a built-in limit, use Avatar Stack.
Cut the list yourself and put the rest in `AvatarGroupCount` as `+3`. The group renders every child it gets; it does not count or hide anyone.
Make the count a button with `interactive` when people can open the rest. Give it an `aria-label` such as `Show 3 more people` and `aria-expanded`.
Place the group on a surface that sets `--surface`, such as a Card. The rings take that colour, so each avatar reads as cut out of the background.
Pick `overlap` for a header or a row where room is short, and `spaced` for a short list where each face should stay whole.
Don't mix avatar sizes in one group. The overlap and the size of the count circle assume one `size` for every avatar.
Don't use a group for a single person, or for a list people should read name by name. Use Avatar, or Person Cell with a name.

components.title: Badge
components.description: A small status or category label in 12 colors and 6 styles.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

parts.name: Badge
parts.description: A short label in a rounded box. `color` picks one of 12 colors and `badgeStyle` one of 6 styles; `size` is `sm` (20 px) or `md` (24 px) and `shape` is `rounded` or `pill`. Rendered as a `<button>` or `<a>` through `render`, it gains hover, focus and press states.

parts.name: Leading mark
parts.description: A Lucide icon as a child, or the `dot`. The icon is 12 px on a small badge and 14 px on a medium one, follows the color of the label, and sits 4 px or 6 px before it.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The children: one short line, 12 px semibold on a small badge and 14 px on a medium one. The badge never wraps and clips what does not fit, so keep the label to a word or two.

parts.name: Remove button
parts.description: A 16 px round button with an X, drawn when `onRemove` is set. It is a separate button with its own name from `removeLabel`; the badge itself stays inert. It is left out when the badge is rendered as a button or link.

parts.name: BadgeCell
parts.description: A Badge for a table cell, made from a `label` string, with the `light_border` style by default.

parts.name: BadgeCounter
parts.description: A count next to a label, or on the corner of an icon button with `overlay`. The tones are `neutral`, `brand` and `danger`. Counts above `max` (99) read `99+`, and an overlay counter hides itself at zero.

parts.name: BadgeIndicator
parts.description: A small signal: `unread`, presence (`online`, `away`, `busy`, `offline`) or a symbol (`check`, `warning`, `lock`). Each kind has its own shape, not only its own color, and carries an accessible name.

parts.name: BadgeProcessing
parts.description: A running operation and its result: `pending` (a turning spinner), `success` or `error`. The label always names the state.

parts.name: Chip
parts.description: An interactive pill that filters, selects or opens a list. Selection shows as the indigo tint and a mark, never as color alone.

parts.name: EntityChip
parts.description: A person, team or workspace as a pill: a 24 px mark (an avatar, an image, a flag) before the name, and an optional remove button.

parts.name: TokenChip
parts.description: One entry inside a multi-value field, such as an email address. An invalid token gets a warning icon and the red tint; the field names the error.

items.text: Use a Badge for a short status or category on a row, card or heading: `Paid`, `Draft`, `Beta`. For the change in a number use Trend Chip, and for a message people have to read use Alert.
Give each status one `color` and keep it wherever that status appears. Write the status in the label as well, so color is never the only cue.
Use `light` or `light_border` in tables and lists, and keep the solid `plain` style for the one badge that should stand out.
Pass `render={<button />}` when the badge does something. Only a `<button>` or `<a>` gets the pointer cursor, the hover ring and the focus ring.
Put an overlay counter or indicator on the corner of a `relative` button and put the count in the name of that button, for example `Notifications, 3 unread`. The counter itself stays decorative.
Use `Chip` for a filter or a choice. It announces its selected state and shows a mark as well as the tint.
Don't use a Badge as a selection control. A removable tag takes `onRemove`; anything that selects or opens a list is a `Chip`.
Don't recolor a badge with classes or hex values. Every `color` and `badgeStyle` pair is measured for AA contrast in light and dark mode.
Don't put two badges on one heading, or a badge on every row of a list. A badge that is everywhere says nothing.

components.title: Breadcrumb
components.description: Shows the user's location in a hierarchy, in the `plain`, `contained` or `underline` look.

keyboard: Tab between the links
aria: nav with aria-label "breadcrumb"; the current page has aria-current="page"; separators are hidden from screen readers

parts.name: Breadcrumb
parts.description: The `<nav>` landmark named `breadcrumb`. `variant` sets the look of every part: `plain`, `contained` (the old name `border` still works) or `underline`. `density` (`default` 36 px rows, `compact` 28 px) switches the trail to the sized layout, on one line.

parts.name: BreadcrumbList
parts.description: The ordered list `<ol>` of items and separators. In the `contained` look it draws the border and the surface, in the `underline` look the line below. Without `density` it wraps onto a second line when the trail runs out of room.

parts.name: BreadcrumbItem
parts.description: One step of the trail, an `<li>` holding a link or, at the end, the current page.

parts.name: BreadcrumbLink
parts.description: A level above the current page, an `<a>` that takes `href`. It can hold an icon before the text. `truncated` limits it to 160 px with an ellipsis and the full name as `title`.

parts.name: BreadcrumbSeparator
parts.description: An `<li>` between two items, hidden from screen readers. It shows a chevron, a slash with `type="slash"`, or your own icon as children.

parts.name: BreadcrumbEllipsis
parts.description: A button that stands for hidden middle levels. Use it as the trigger of a Popover that lists them; it shows an open state from `aria-expanded`.

parts.name: BreadcrumbPage
parts.description: The current page as text, not a link, marked with `aria-current="page"`. `truncated` works like on the link.

parts.name: BreadcrumbSiblingTrigger
parts.description: A separate button beside a link that opens a list of sibling pages. The link still navigates; the chevron turns when the list is open.

parts.name: BreadcrumbRestricted
parts.description: A level the person cannot open. It stays in the trail with a lock, is focusable and explains itself through its `title`.

parts.name: BreadcrumbLoading
parts.description: A quiet placeholder for the current level while its name loads. It has `role="status"`; there is no spinner.

items.text: Use a Breadcrumb on nested pages, such as one project's settings, so people see where they are and can step back up. For switching between sibling views, use Tabs.
End the trail with `BreadcrumbPage`, not a link. It carries `aria-current="page"`, so screen readers announce where the person is.
Put a `BreadcrumbSeparator` between items yourself; the list does not add them. Each one sits in its own `<li>` and is hidden from assistive technology.
Pass `density` to get the sized layout: 36 px rows with hover underline, pressed fill and focus ring. Without it the trail is the small inline list.
Collapse deep trails to the root, the parent and the current page. Put the hidden levels behind a `BreadcrumbEllipsis` that opens a list of links, in their real order.
Keep a restricted level visible with `BreadcrumbRestricted` instead of removing it, so the trail stays truthful.
Show the trail as one link to the parent page below 360 px of width.
Don't link the current page or set `aria-current` on a link by hand. `BreadcrumbPage` already marks the last step and is not clickable.
Don't show a spinner while the current name loads. Use `BreadcrumbLoading`, a quiet placeholder with the right accessible name.
Don't use a breadcrumb as the only way to move around. It shows the path to the page, not every page there is.

components.title: Button
components.description: The main action trigger, in 11 variants, 2 shapes and 5 sizes.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: pending
props.description: Shows a spinner in place of the leading icon and ignores presses. The button stays focusable and keeps its colour (it is not disabled).

props.name: phase
props.description: Async feedback: pending shows a spinner, success a check, error a retry icon. The label is yours (for example Saving…, Saved, Retry). Keep the width constant with a fixed width on the button so it does not jump between phases.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

keyboard: Enter / Space: activate
aria: Renders a native <button>; with `render` set to another element pass nativeButton={false} so the button role and keys are kept
a11y.notes: Disabled buttons leave the tab order unless focusableWhenDisabled is set.

parts.name: Button
parts.description: The clickable element: a native `<button>` that fits its content. `variant` picks the look, `size` the height (32 to 48 px at the default density), `shape` rounded or pill. `pending` shows a spinner in place of the leading icon and ignores presses; `phase` runs the async feedback Save changes, Saving…, Saved, Retry.

parts.name: Leading icon
parts.description: An icon before the label. Mark it `data-icon="inline-start"` so the padding on that side is 2 px tighter. It is 16 px at `sm` and `md`, 20 px at `lg`, 24 px at `xl` and `2xl`, and is replaced by the spinner while the button is pending.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The text, in 14 px medium (16 px at `xl`, 18 px at `2xl`). Write a verb and its object, such as `Save changes`, and keep it on one line.

parts.name: Trailing icon
parts.description: An icon after the label, for a direction such as an arrow or a chevron. Mark it `data-icon="inline-end"`.

parts.name: ButtonCell
parts.description: A small plain button for a table cell, for a secondary action in a row. It takes the label as `children` and `onClick`.

items.text: Use a Button for an action on the current page: save, send, open a dialog. A move to another page is a link: pass `render={<a href=… />}` together with `nativeButton={false}`.

Give each view one `primary` or `gradient` button for its main action. Every other action is `plain` or a link; an icon-only control inside a row, toolbar, field or card is an `IconButton` with `ghost`.
Label it with a verb and its object: `Save changes`, `Invite member`. A destructive button repeats the action it runs; the button next to it says `Cancel`.

Show the result of an async action on the button itself with `phase`: `Save changes`, `Saving…`, `Saved`, `Retry`. Give the button a fixed width so it does not jump between phases, and put the reason for an error in a message next to it.
Give an icon-only control an `aria-label` and use `IconButton` for it, not a Button with an icon and no label.
Don't use `outline` for ordinary secondary actions. In WunderUI the secondary button is `plain`; `outline` is the indigo-rimmed accent for the rare case that needs one.
Don't set heights or paddings by hand (`h-9`, `px-6`). Pick a `size`: the sizes read the density tokens, so compact and comfortable both stay right.
Don't make `destructive` the default button. The destructive action says what it does (`Delete workspace`) and sits next to a plain `Cancel`.
Don't disable a button without saying why. Where the reason is not obvious, show it in a message or a tooltip next to the button, or keep the button enabled and explain the error after the press.

keyboard: Enter / Space: activate

parts.name: IconButton
parts.description: A native `<button>` that holds one icon in a square (`rounded`) or a circle. It has no visible text, so its name comes from `aria-label`. `pending` puts a spinner in the same square and ignores presses; `phase` runs the async feedback idle, pending, success and error in the same square; `expanded` marks a trigger whose menu or panel is open.

parts.name: Icon
parts.description: The child: a Lucide icon at 1.5 stroke. It is 16 px at `sm`, 18 at `md`, 20 at `lg`, 22 at `xl` and 24 at `2xl`, and takes the colour of the text. The whole square is the hit area.

parts.name: IconButtonTextCell
parts.description: A table cell with a small plain icon button beside a label. Its `label` prop becomes the name of the button and falls back to `Action`.

items.text: Use an IconButton for a frequent action whose icon is unmistakable: close, edit, more options. When the icon alone could be misread, use a Button with a text label.
Give every IconButton an `aria-label` that names the action: `Delete invoice`, not `Trash`. A tooltip is extra help, not the name.

Set `variant="plain"` for a secondary icon action with its own box and `ghost` for an icon-only control that sits inside a row, toolbar, field or card. The default is `primary`, and a view has one primary action.
Pass `label` to IconButtonTextCell. Without it every row's button is announced as `Action`.

Show a running action with `pending` or `phase` instead of swapping the icon yourself. The square keeps its size, a press is ignored while it runs, and the button stays focusable. Change the `aria-label` with the phase: `Copy link`, `Copying link`, `Link copied`.
Put the count of a badge into the name: `Notifications, 3 unread`. Draw the counter with `BadgeCounter overlay` on a `relative` wrapper and mark it `aria-hidden`; the badge is not a second button.
Use `expanded` on a trigger that opens a menu or a panel, and a `Toggle` with one stable name for a state that stays on, such as Favorite. Pressed (the click) and selected look different.
Don't use `sm` or `md` as the only control on a touch screen. Pick `xl` or `2xl`, which reach the 44 px hit area the polish rules ask for on touch.

components.title: Button Group
components.description: A row of connected buttons sharing borders and outer corners, for view switchers or segmented actions.

props.name: orientation
props.description: "horizontal" puts the buttons in a row, "vertical" stacks them with shared edges.

props.name: children
props.description: The label of the action part.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables both parts.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: groupClassName
props.description: Class names for the group wrapping both parts.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading icon of the action part. Decorative.

props.name: menu
props.description: The entries of the menu: DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuSeparator and so on.

props.name: menuLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the menu part. Default "More actions".

props.name: menuProps
props.description: Props for the menu popup, for example `align`. Default `align="end"`.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: onAction
props.description: Runs when the action part is pressed.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state of the menu.

props.name: pending
props.description: Shows a spinner in place of the leading icon and ignores presses. The button stays focusable and keeps its colour (it is not disabled).

props.name: phase
props.description: Async feedback: pending shows a spinner, success a check, error a retry icon. The label is yours (for example Saving…, Saved, Retry). Keep the width constant with a fixed width on the button so it does not jump between phases.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: size
props.description: Same sizes as the Button. The Figma "Medium 40" is `size="lg"`; the default stays the Button default `md`.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: variant
props.description: "plain" (default) is a white button with a border, "solid" the primary fill.

parts.name: ButtonGroup
parts.description: A `role="group"` row, or a stack with `orientation="vertical"`, that joins its children. Only the two outer ends keep their corners: left and right in a row, top and bottom in a stack. `shape` is `rounded` or `pill`. Name it with `aria-label`.

parts.name: Button
parts.description: Each direct child, usually a plain Button or Icon Button of the same size. The group sets its corners and overlaps its border with the neighbour's. The focused one moves on top, so its focus ring is not covered.

parts.name: Shared edge
parts.description: One border between two neighbours: the next button overlaps the border of the previous one by 1 px, so two buttons never draw a double line.

parts.name: SplitButton
parts.description: A group of two parts: the action part with its label and an optional icon, and the menu part with a chevron that opens a Dropdown Menu. Each part has its own hover, pressed and open fill, and there is no focus ring: keyboard focus shows through the fill.

items.text: Use a Button Group for a few related actions that belong together, such as share, export and print, or zoom in and zoom out. For one choice that stays selected, use a Segment or a Radio Button Group.
Give the group an `aria-label` that names what the buttons do together, such as `Zoom`. It already has `role="group"`, but no name.
Use the same `variant` and `size` on every button inside, and plain buttons in most cases. The shared borders only line up when the buttons have the same height and border.
Name every icon-only button in a group with `aria-label`, and keep to one kind of content: all text, all icons, or all icon and text.
Use a Split Button when one action is far more common than its alternatives, and put the alternatives in its menu.
Don't wrap the buttons in extra elements. Corners and overlaps are set on direct children only, so a wrapper breaks the joined edges.
Don't put a primary or gradient button into the group. A view has one main action, and the joined edges present the buttons as equals.
Don't use a group as a selector. Joined buttons look like a choice, but a group of actions has no selected state: use a Segment for exactly one choice.

components.title: Card
components.description: A bordered container for grouping related content.

parts.name: Card
parts.description: The surface in `default`, `elevated` or `outlined` style. It has 16 px of padding on every side and 16 px between its parts (12 px in the small size), clips its content to a 16 px corner radius and sets `--surface` for the parts inside. `orientation="horizontal"` puts the media at the left, `interactive` makes the whole card one target with hover, pressed and focus states, and `selected` shows the tint surface, border and text of a chosen card.

parts.name: CardMedia
parts.description: An image area flush with the top edge (flush with the left edge in a horizontal card). Put an `` inside to fill it; empty, it shows an image placeholder. `ratio` sets 16:9, 4:3, 1:1 or 3:1 instead of the fixed 160 px height, and `missing` shows the "No preview available" fallback.

parts.name: CardHeader
parts.description: A grid for the title, the description and an optional action on the right. `leading` adds an icon tile or an avatar at the left.

parts.name: CardTitle
parts.description: The title of the card. It renders a `<div>`, so put a heading element inside when the card opens a section of the page.

parts.name: CardDescription
parts.description: Secondary text under the title, in the secondary text colour.

parts.name: CardAction
parts.description: Sits top right in the header beside the title and the description, for a menu button or one small button. It stays there however long the title runs.

parts.name: CardContent
parts.description: The body, with the side padding of the card. Anything goes in it: text, a list, a form, a chart.

parts.name: CardFooter
parts.description: A row of buttons with a line above it. `layout` sets `end` (right-aligned), `between` (a note left, actions right), `stretch` (equal buttons) or `stacked` (full-width buttons, primary first); `divider={false}` removes the line. The card drops its own bottom padding when a footer is present.

parts.name: CardBody
parts.description: The text column of a horizontal card, next to the media. It carries the vertical padding that a horizontal card does not have itself.

parts.name: CardIcon
parts.description: An icon tile for the `leading` slot of the header: a tint surface, a rim of the same hue and the icon in the tint text colour.

parts.name: CardMeta
parts.description: A row for a date, a status, a category or the people, in small secondary text. It wraps on a narrow card.

parts.name: CardIndicator
parts.description: The radio or checkbox mark at the top right of a selectable card. It is decorative: the card or its trigger carries the role and `aria-checked`.

parts.name: CardTrigger
parts.description: A button that covers the whole card, for a card that also holds other controls. It is the card's only focus stop; raise the other controls above it with `relative z-10`.

parts.name: CardFeedback
parts.description: The data states of the whole card: `loading` (a skeleton like the content), `empty`, `error` and `denied`, each with an optional title, description and action.

parts.name: CardBanner
parts.description: A strip flush at the top of a card: `refreshing` while the data stays visible, or `error` with a Retry when the last data stays visible.

parts.name: CardDragHandle
parts.description: The grip for cards in a sortable list such as a board. Every drag needs a keyboard alternative, such as a Move to menu.

items.text: Use a Card to group the content of one thing, such as a project, a plan or a settings section. For a row with an icon, a title and meta, use Item Card; for a single number, Metric Card; when there is nothing to show yet, Empty State.
Leave the padding to the card. The default size has the same 16 px inset as the chart, stat and metric cards, so use `size="sm"` for dense grids instead of overriding `p-*` classes.
Put a menu button or one small button in `CardAction`. It stays top right however long the title runs.
Make the whole card the target with `interactive`, and give it a role (`link`, `button` or `radio`) and a name with `aria-label`.
When a card holds other controls, use `interactive tabIndex={-1}` with a `CardTrigger` as the one target and raise the other controls with `relative z-10`.
Use plain buttons in `CardFooter` when cards repeat in a grid. A view has one main action, and a gradient button on every card leaves none.
Show data states on the card itself: `CardFeedback` for loading, empty, error and no access, and `CardBanner` when the old data stays visible while it refreshes or after a refresh failed.
Pick the footer layout by its content: `end` for a normal row of actions, `between` when a note sits beside them, `stretch` and `stacked` for a narrow card.
Don't put a button inside a card that is itself a button or a link. Use a `CardTrigger`, or keep the card static.
Don't set `bg-white` or a hex colour on a card. `bg-card` follows the theme and dark mode, and the parts inside read it through `--surface`.

parts.name: Checkbox
parts.description: The box: a 16 px square with a 4 px radius and a `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked`. Checked or indeterminate it is filled with the brand colour (`appearance="neutral"`: black in light mode, white in dark). Its hit area reaches 12 px to the sides and 8 px above and below the box, and `aria-invalid` turns the border and the focus ring red.

parts.name: Check indicator
parts.description: The check, or a dash while `indeterminate`. The stroke of the check is drawn in when the box is ticked. Checkbox renders it; you do not pass it.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The text that names the box. Pass `label` and it is joined to the box with `htmlFor` inside one `<label>`, so the whole row is the click target; or use the title of a Selector Item. `description` adds a second line under it in 12 px tertiary text. A link in the label keeps its own colour and click. Without a label, give the box an `aria-label`.

parts.name: Error message
parts.description: A line under the row in 12 px type in the error colour, indented to the text (24 px). `error` renders it outside the label, so it is not part of the box's name, sets `aria-invalid` on the box and points `aria-describedby` at it.

items.text: Use a Checkbox for an on or off choice in a form, or to pick several items from a list. For a setting that takes effect at once use Switch, and for one choice out of several use Radio Group.
Give every checkbox a visible label with the `label` prop. It is joined to the box, so a click on the text toggles it and a screen reader announces the label with the value.
Write the label as the choice itself: `Email me about new releases`. Put a sentence of detail in `description` under the label.
Use `indeterminate` on a select-all box while only some rows are chosen. Work it out from the rows and state its scope: `Select all acts on the 5 members shown`.
State the rule of a group above it, and put the error under the group, not on one row: `Choose at least two topics.`
Pass `error` on a required box only after the first try to continue, and say in the message what to do: `Accept the terms to create your account.`
Don't import CheckboxField in new code. It is a deprecated alias of Checkbox; use Checkbox with the same props.
Don't build a checkbox from a styled `<div>`. The component already handles Space, the focus ring and the larger hit area around the small box.
Don't use a checkbox for a setting that applies at once. A box looks like part of a form that is saved later; use a Switch.
Don't offer indeterminate as a choice. It only displays a partial selection; people can never pick it.
Don't show the error before the first try. A red box on load reads as a mistake the person has not made yet.

components.title: Switch
components.description: A toggle control for a binary setting.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Checked-track colour: `brand`, `neutral` (inverse black/white) or `muted` (quiet grey).

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether the switch is currently active. To render an uncontrolled switch, use the `defaultChecked` prop instead.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Whether the switch is initially active. To render a controlled switch, use the `checked` prop instead.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

props.name: form
props.description: Identifies the form that owns the hidden input. Useful when the switch is rendered outside the form.

props.name: id
props.description: The id of the hidden input element. When `nativeButton` is `true`, the id is applied to the root element.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: A ref to access the hidden `<input>` element.

props.name: name
props.description: Identifies the field when a form is submitted.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `true` if the rendered element is a native button.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Event handler called when the switch is activated or deactivated.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the user should be unable to activate or deactivate the switch.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: required
props.description: Whether the user must activate the switch before submitting a form.

props.name: saving
props.description: Pending save: the handle shows a spinner, the switch is `aria-busy` and ignores clicks until it is cleared.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: uncheckedValue
props.description: The value submitted with the form when the switch is off. By default, unchecked switches do not submit any value, matching native checkbox behavior.

props.name: value
props.description: The value submitted with the form when the switch is on. By default, switch submits the "on" value, matching native checkbox behavior.

keyboard: Space / Enter: turn on or off
aria: role=switch with aria-checked
Needs a label: Label or Field

parts.name: Switch
parts.description: The track: a `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`, 32 by 18 px in the `default` size and 24 by 14 px in `sm`. Off it is grey; on it takes the brand colour, `neutral` (black or white) or `muted`. Its hit area reaches 12 px to the sides and 8 px above and below.

parts.name: Thumb
parts.description: The round knob. It slides over with a slight overshoot and reverses mid-way when the switch is clicked again. While `saving` it shows a spinner. Switch renders it; you do not pass it.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The text that names the setting, a `Label` with `htmlFor` that matches the `id` of the switch, or the title of a Selector Item. A click on it toggles the switch. Name the setting, never the state.

parts.name: SwitchItemCell
parts.description: A table cell that puts a Switch and its text in one `<label>`, so the text also toggles it.

items.text: Use a Switch for one setting that is on or off and takes effect at once, such as email notifications. For a choice that is saved later with a form, use a Checkbox.
Give every switch a visible label and join it with `htmlFor` and `id`. A click on the text then toggles it, and a screen reader announces the name with `on` or `off`.
Name the setting, not the state: `Email notifications`, not `On`. The `switch` role already tells screen readers whether it is on.
Pass `saving` while a request runs. The knob shows a spinner and clicks are ignored until the save ends.
When a save fails, set the switch back to its previous value and say so in a message with a retry: `Couldn't save. Try again.`
Use `size="sm"` in dense rows such as table cells, and the default size in forms and settings.
Don't mark a switch `aria-invalid`. It has no wrong value; a failed save is an error of the request, so put it in the message.
Don't use a Switch to choose between two named options such as Monthly and Yearly. That is a choice, not on or off; use a Radio Group.
Don't ask people to press a Save button after a Switch. A switch that waits for a button is a Checkbox.

components.title: Radio Group
components.description: A set of mutually exclusive options.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The uncontrolled value of the radio button that should be initially selected. To render a controlled radio group, use the `value` prop instead.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

props.name: form
props.description: Identifies the form that owns the radio inputs. Useful when the radio group is rendered outside the form.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: A ref to access the hidden input element.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the whole group invalid (sets aria-invalid on the group; same as passing aria-invalid).

props.name: name
props.description: Identifies the field when a form is submitted.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Callback fired when the value changes.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the user should be unable to select a different radio button in the group.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: required
props.description: Whether the user must choose a value before submitting a form.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: value
props.description: The controlled value of the radio item that should be currently selected. To render an uncontrolled radio group, use the `defaultValue` prop instead.

props.name: value
props.description: The unique identifying value of the radio in a group.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: A ref to access the hidden input element.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `true` if the rendered element is a native button.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the user should be unable to select the radio button.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: required
props.description: Whether the user must choose a value before submitting a form.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: tone
props.description: `tint` for a radio that sits on a tint surface when selected (a selected option card): the mark takes the tint colours of the same hue, like the Choice Button. `default` is the plain brand radio on a white surface.

keyboard: Arrow keys: move to and select the next or previous option
Tab: into and out of the group
aria: role=radiogroup with role=radio items; label the group (Fieldset legend or aria-label)

parts.name: RadioGroup
parts.description: The group: a `div` with `role="radiogroup"` that holds the chosen `value`. It lays the options out in a grid with an 8 px gap; add classes for a row. Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and set `invalid` to mark the whole group.

parts.name: RadioGroupItem
parts.description: One round option, 16 px across, with its own `value`. Its hit area reaches 12 px to the sides and 8 px above and below the circle, so a near miss still selects it.

parts.name: Dot
parts.description: The 6 px dot shown while the option is chosen. RadioGroupItem renders it; you do not pass it.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The text that names the option, a `Label` with `htmlFor` that matches the `id` of the radio, or the title of a Selector Item. A click on it chooses the option.

parts.name: Description
parts.description: A line of detail under the label, in secondary text, such as when an order arrives. It is not part of the label, so it does not widen the name.

items.text: Use a Radio Group when people choose exactly one option from a short list they should see at once. For a long list use a menu, and for options shown as buttons use a Radio Button Group.
Name the group with a visible label and `aria-labelledby`, or with an `aria-label`. A screen reader announces the name when focus enters the group.
Give every option a visible label and join it with `htmlFor` and `id`, so a click on the text also chooses it.
Choose a sensible default with `defaultValue` when one exists. Once an option is chosen it cannot be cleared, so an empty start only helps when the choice is required.
Put the error on the group: set `invalid` and write one message under it. Do not repeat the message on every row.
Use Selector Item with a RadioGroupItem as its `control` when each option needs a title, a description and a price, such as plans.
Don't use two radios for on and off. A single setting that is on or off is a Switch or a Checkbox.
Don't validate before the first try. A red group on load reads as a mistake that was not made yet.
Don't split one choice into several groups, or put an unrelated control between the options. People expect the arrow keys to stay inside one group.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The visible name of the field. Pass `label` and the input is joined to it with `htmlFor` (the id comes from `useId` unless you give one). A click on it focuses the field. `optional` adds the tag `(optional)`, `labelTrailing` puts a note or a link on the label row. A search field that has no room for a label takes an `aria-label` instead.

parts.name: Input
parts.description: The single-line field: a native `<input>` with a 1 px border and an 8 px corner. Its height comes from `size` and the density tokens (32, 36 or 40 px). With content inside it, an `InputGroup` draws the border and the focus ring instead, and the input in it is transparent. Without any of the field props it renders this bare `<input>` and nothing around it.

parts.name: Leading content
parts.description: An icon or a short text before the value, passed as `leading`: a mail icon, `https://`. It is drawn in an `InputGroupAddon`, is not interactive and sits in the tertiary text colour.

parts.name: Trailing content
parts.description: A unit, a shortcut or a small button after the value, passed as `trailing`: `USD`, a key hint, copy. `revealable` adds the show-or-hide button of a password field here. A button you compose yourself is a 32 px `IconButton` that sits 2 px inside the field and has a 6 px corner, so it is concentric with the 8 px corner of the field.

parts.name: Helper and error text
parts.description: A line under the field in 12 px type: `helper` with the rule, or `error` with what to do. The error replaces the helper; it never stands next to it. Both are joined to the input with `aria-describedby`, and `error` sets `aria-invalid`.

parts.name: Validation tooltip
parts.description: Shows the browser's message for `required`, `type="email"` or `pattern` when the form is submitted, and clears once the user types or leaves the field.

items.text: Use an Input for one line of free text: a name, an email address, a search term. Several lines go in a Textarea; a choice from a known list goes in a Native Select or a Combobox.
Give every Input a visible label with the `label` prop. A placeholder disappears with the first keystroke and is not a name. A search field may use `aria-label`.
Pick the `type` and `autoComplete` that match the value (`email`, `password`, `cc-number`). The browser then offers the right keyboard and fills the field in for the person.
Mark a wrong value with `error` and say in the message what to do: `Enter an email address like name@company.com`, not `Invalid input`. Keep what the person typed.
Show the error after the person leaves the field or sends the form, not on the first keystroke. A red field on load reads as a mistake that has not been made yet.
Keep the label a noun (`Work email`) and put a rule in `helper` below it as a full sentence.
Use `revealable` on every `type="password"` field that a person types by hand, and set `autoComplete` to `current-password` on sign-in or `new-password` on sign-up.
Don't import TextField or PasswordField in new code. They are deprecated aliases of Input; use Input with the same props.
Don't use a placeholder as the label, and don't put the format example only there: it is gone once the field is filled.
Don't size a field with `h-*` classes. Use `size` (`sm`, `default`, `lg`): a field and a Button of the same size line up, in both densities.
Don't use `disabled` for a value people need to read or copy. A read-only field can be focused and copied; a disabled one cannot, and it is dimmed.
Don't use `type="number"` for codes, phone numbers or card numbers. They are text with `inputMode="numeric"`, so leading zeros survive.

Its minimum height comes from `size` and the density tokens (72, 96 or 128 px), and the text scrolls inside once it is longer. parts.name: Character counter
parts.description: Shows `length/maxLength` in the bottom-right corner when `showCount` and `maxLength` are both set. The field adds room below the text for it, so the counter never covers a line.

parts.name: Resize handle
parts.description: The browser's handle in the bottom-right corner, which drags the field taller. It is on by default (`resize-y`); `resize-none` removes it.

parts.name: Helper and error text

items.text: Use a Textarea for free text over several lines: a message, a description, feedback. One line goes in an Input; formatted text goes in a Rich Text Editor.
Give it a visible label with the `label` prop. A placeholder disappears with the first keystroke and is not a name.
Set `maxLength` together with `showCount` when there is a limit. The counter appears only when both are set, and the field stops accepting text at the limit.
Say in `error` what to do (`Enter at least 20 characters`) and keep what the person typed. Show it after the person leaves the field or sends the form.
Pick the size for the text you expect: `sm` for a note, `default` for a message, `lg` for a description. People can still drag the field taller.
Mark the exception, not the rule: when most fields are needed, pass `optional` on the few that are not instead of a star on every other label.
Don't import TextareaField in new code. It is a deprecated alias of Textarea; use Textarea with the same props.
Don't size it with `rows` or `h-*` classes. Pick `size` (`sm`, `default`, `lg`): the heights read the density tokens, so compact and comfortable both stay right.
Don't hide the counter and cut the text off silently. A limit the person cannot see feels like a bug.
Don't put a chat composer's buttons next to the field by hand. Put the field and its buttons in one box that owns the border and the focus ring.

parts.name: Progress
parts.description: The root: a `div` with `role="progressbar"`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuenow`. Children such as the label render above the bar. `valuePosition` prints the value at the right or left of the bar, below it, or in a bubble above or below it.

parts.name: ProgressLabel
parts.description: Names the task. Progress points `aria-labelledby` at it. Without a label, give Progress an `aria-label`.

parts.name: ProgressIndicator
parts.description: The fill, in the brand colour. It is drawn at full width and scaled to the value, and it glides to a new value over `duration-ambient`. Progress already renders it; with a null value it is drawn without a width.

parts.name: ProgressTrack
parts.description: The grey bar behind the fill: 6 px high and fully rounded. Progress already renders it; you only need it for a custom layout.

parts.name: ProgressValue
parts.description: Prints the formatted value, a percent of the range by default, in tabular figures. It is hidden from assistive technology, because the bar already announces its value. With `valuePosition` it sits beside or below the bar, or in a bubble.

items.text: Use Progress for a task that runs to completion: an upload, an import, a run of setup steps. For a fixed value inside a range, such as storage used, use Meter.
Name the bar with `ProgressLabel` or `aria-label`, such as `Uploading report.pdf`. Screen readers then say what is progressing, not only the number.
Add `ProgressValue` when the number matters. It formats the value and uses tabular figures, so the text does not jump while it counts.

Put the value where it is read first: `valuePosition="right"` for a compact row, `"bottom"` when the bar spans the full width, `"tooltip-top"` or `"tooltip-bottom"` when the number should follow the end of the fill.
Set `max` to the number of steps when the task has steps, and pass the steps done as `value`: `value={3} max={5}`. The bar then needs no sum of its own.
When you print your own text, pass `getAriaValueText` as well, so a screen reader hears the same words: `3 of 5 steps`. Otherwise it announces the percent.
Say a failure in words next to the bar and offer the next action: `Failed, retry`. The bar keeps the value where the task stopped.
Don't animate the width of the fill yourself. The indicator already scales with a transform on the `duration-ambient` timing.
Don't use an indeterminate bar for a long wait on its own. It draws no fill and no motion, so pair it with a Spinner or a message.
Don't show a bar for a measured value such as storage used. It would announce a task that is never finished. Use Meter.

keyboard: Arrow keys: step
Shift + Arrow / Page Up / Page Down: largeStep (default 10)
Home / End: minimum / maximum
aria: role=slider with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax
Pass aria-label or aria-labelledby

parts.name: Slider
parts.description: Holds the value and draws one thumb per value: a number gives one thumb, an array of two gives a range. Its `aria-label` moves to the thumbs. `handle` picks the thumb (`circle`, `circle-neutral`, `grip-bars`, `grip-dots`), `centered` fills from the middle of a bipolar scale, `bubble` shows the value above the thumb (`"always"` keeps it visible), `marks` adds ticks, `invalid` turns the fill and the thumb red and `error` draws the error text under it.

parts.name: SliderLabel
parts.description: A visible name for the slider, linked to the thumbs. Put it, with the value, in a row inside `Slider`. `SliderField` draws its own label.

parts.name: SliderValue
parts.description: Shows the current value or range on the right in tabular figures.

parts.name: SliderControl
parts.description: The area that takes pointer input, a little taller than the track so it is easy to hit. Slider already renders it.

parts.name: SliderTrack
parts.description: The grey bar the thumbs travel on, 6 px thick, horizontal or vertical. Slider already renders it.

parts.name: SliderIndicator
parts.description: The filled part of the track up to the value, or between the two thumbs of a range. A centred slider draws its own fill from the origin.

parts.name: SliderThumb
parts.description: The handle people drag or move with the arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down. It is the focusable element screen readers announce. Slider renders one per value. It fills with the page tone on hover and the subtle tone while dragging; `thumbClassName` on Slider reaches every thumb.

parts.name: SliderBubble
parts.description: The value bubble above the thumb, decorative. It fades in on focus and while dragging, and close range thumbs share one.

parts.name: SliderMarks
parts.description: Tick marks on the scale, decorative. Label only the marks that need a word, never every step.

parts.name: SliderField
parts.description: A slider as a form field: label that names the thumbs, current value with its unit, optional limits, number inputs, and a helper or error text that describes the thumbs. The error turns the slider red.

parts.name: SliderInput
parts.description: A number field that follows the slider in the English number format and clamps and snaps when left.

parts.name: SliderRangeInputs
parts.description: Two number fields for a range; the lower value may not pass the upper one.

items.text: Use a Slider when the rough position matters more than the exact figure: volume, a price range, a zoom level. For an exact number, use a Number Field.
Use `SliderField` for every slider in a form or a panel, so the label and the current value always sit next to the thumb. Add `showInput` when exact values matter.
Name every slider: `SliderField` takes a `label`, a bare `Slider` takes `aria-label`. For a range the thumbs are announced as `Budget, minimum` and `Budget, maximum`.
Set `step` to the precision people need and keep `largeStep` at about ten steps. Shift with an arrow key and Page Up and Page Down move by `largeStep`.
Pass an array such as `defaultValue={[20, 80]}` for a range. Slider draws one thumb per value.
Label only the marks that need a word, such as the first, the default and the last. A label on every tick is noise.
Show an error through `error`: the fill and the thumb turn red, and the text under the slider is announced. Say what to change: `Choose at least 10%.`
Give the reason in the helper text when a slider is disabled. The value stays readable, and people should not have to guess why they cannot change it.
Don't add SliderThumb children for a range. The array decides how many thumbs there are.
Don't rely on colour alone for an error. The red fill comes with the error text and `aria-invalid`.
Don't use a vertical slider without a height. It fills the height of its container, so a column without one gives the track nothing to stretch to.
Don't use a Slider for a choice between a few named options. Use a Segmented Control or a Radio Group.

components.title: Pagination
components.description: Page navigation with Prev/Next and numbered pages, or a simple "Page X of Y" mode.

props.name: currentStyle
props.description: Figma "Current style": the current page in the brand colour or on a subtle surface. Default "primary".

props.name: shape
props.description: "pill" rounds every button fully (Figma Shape=Pill). Default "rounded".

props.name: showEdges
props.description: Adds "First page" and "Last page" as their own buttons at the two ends.

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: Called with a valid page (a whole number from 1 to `pageCount`).

props.name: buttonLabel
props.description: Text of the button. Default "Go".

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Default "Go to page".

props.name: value
props.description: Current page size.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Default "Rows per page".

props.name: options
props.description: Choices in the menu. Default 10, 25, 50, 100.

props.name: shape
props.description: "pill" rounds both buttons fully. Default "rounded".

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Shown instead of the default message while `status="error"`.

props.name: itemCount
props.description: Rows on the current page, for an unknown total or a short last page. Defaults to `pageSize`.

props.name: noun
props.description: Singular noun for the total, "result" in "248 results".

props.name: nounPlural
props.description: Plural noun, defaults to `noun` + "s".

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Makes the error state show a "Retry" button.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page, 1-based. Together with `pageSize` it gives the range "1–10".

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Rows per page.

props.name: status
props.description: "loading" shows a skeleton, "error" says the count failed and offers a retry.

props.name: total
props.description: Total number of rows. Leave it out when the total is not known.

keyboard: Tab between the page links, Enter to open
aria: nav with aria-label "Pagination"; the current page has aria-current

parts.name: Pagination
parts.description: A `<nav>` named `Pagination`: Prev and Next with numbered page buttons between them. It is controlled: you hold `page` and change it in `onPageChange`. It takes a `shape` of `rounded` or `pill`, a `currentStyle` of `primary` or `subtle`, and `showEdges` for first and last page buttons.

parts.name: Edge buttons
parts.description: The first-page and last-page buttons at the two ends, shown with `showEdges`. Each is an icon button named First page or Last page.

parts.name: Prev and Next
parts.description: Text buttons with a chevron. Prev is disabled on the first page and Next on the last. Below 640 px the text hides and the chevron stays; the text is still read by screen readers.

parts.name: Page button
parts.description: A numbered button that goes to its page. The row always shows the first page, the last page and the pages around the current one.

parts.name: Current page
parts.description: The page you are on, marked with `aria-current="page"`. `primary` fills it with the brand colour, `subtle` sets it on a quiet surface.

parts.name: Ellipsis
parts.description: Stands for the pages that are folded away. It is plain text, not a button.

parts.name: PaginationSimple
parts.description: The compact form: Previous and Next with a `Page X of Y` label between them, for narrow spaces. It takes the same `shape`.

parts.name: PaginationSummary
parts.description: The count line: a range of a total (`21–30 of 248`), the total alone, a range without a total, a loading skeleton, or an error with a Retry button.

parts.name: PaginationPageSize
parts.description: A labelled select for the number of rows per page. Its label is the accessible name of the select.

parts.name: PaginationJump
parts.description: A labelled number field with a Go button. Enter or Go jumps to the page; a value outside 1 to `pageCount` shows an error under the row.

items.text: Keep `page` in state and load the matching rows in `onPageChange`. Pages count from 1, and `pageCount` is the total number of pages.
Show where people are with PaginationSummary next to the pager, such as `21–30 of 248`. When the total is not known, leave `total` out and it says `Showing 21–30`.
Reset `page` to 1 when the page size, a filter or a search changes. Otherwise people can land on a page that no longer exists.
Use `PaginationSimple` where only Previous and Next fit, such as a narrow card or a phone, and keep the count in PaginationSummary above the list.
Don't build page buttons by hand. Pagination already disables Prev on the first page and Next on the last, and marks the current page with `aria-current`.
Don't show a pager for one page. With a `pageCount` of 1 it only shows a lone `1`; hide it instead.
Don't use Pagination for a feed that grows as people read. A list that appends more rows needs a Load more button or an infinite list, not pages.
Don't let `page` leave the range 1 to `pageCount`. Pagination does not clamp it, so a stale `page` shows a row with no current number.

components.title: Separator
components.description: A thin dividing line, horizontal or vertical, solid or dashed.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The orientation of the separator.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

parts.name: Separator
parts.description: A 1 px line with the `separator` role and a matching `aria-orientation`. It is horizontal by default and runs across its container, or vertical with `orientation` and stretches to the height of its row. `dashed` draws it as a dashed border instead of a filled line. It never shrinks in a flex row and has no margin of its own.

items.text: Use a Separator to divide groups inside one surface, such as two sections of a card. For a line with text like `or`, use Divider with Label; inside a toolbar, use ToolbarSeparator.
Place a vertical Separator inside a flex row that has a height. It stretches to the row's height, so a row without one gives the line nothing to stretch to.
Use `dashed` for a lighter break inside one section, such as the line above a total, and the solid line between sections.
Leave the spacing to the layout: a vertical margin such as `my-4` between sections, padding on the rows of a list, and `gap-*` in a row.
Make the line decorative with `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden` when a heading, a list or a group already shows the boundary. Keep the default when the line is the only sign of it.
Don't draw dividers with `border-t` or a hex colour. Separator uses the `--border` token, so it follows the theme and dark mode.
Don't use a Separator to build a panel resizer. It is not focusable and has no value; a resizable layout needs a splitter with keyboard support.
Don't stack a Separator on a border that is already there, such as the last row of a bordered list or the edge of a card. Two lines read as one thick one.

components.title: Divider with Label
components.description: A separator with a centered text label, e.g. for "or" between two sign-in options.

parts.name: DividerWithLabel
parts.description: A full-width row of a line, a label and a second line, separating two groups such as two ways to sign in. `size` is `default` (14 px medium label, 12 px gap) or `sm` (12 px regular label, 16 px gap, for a short word such as `or`); `dashed` draws both lines dashed.

parts.name: Lines
parts.description: Two decorative lines (hidden from assistive technology) that stretch to fill the space on either side of the label. They follow `dashed`. With a label the row has no role; without one the row itself is the single `separator` and the two lines meet in the middle.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The `children`: a word or two such as `or`, centred between the lines in muted text. It can also hold a small plain button, an icon button or an icon.

items.text: Use a Divider with Label between two alternative ways to do the same thing, such as social sign-in and email. For a line without text, use Separator.
Keep the label to one or two words that say how the groups relate: `or`, `or continue with`. Longer text squeezes the lines away.
Place it only between two alternatives, such as sign-in buttons above and an email form below. The label reads as a choice between what is above and what is below.
Use `size="sm"` for a one-word label such as `or` and the default size for a phrase such as `or continue with`.
Put a small plain Button or an IconButton on the line for an action that belongs to the break, such as `Load more`. Give an icon button an `aria-label`.
Use the same word as the buttons around it. If the buttons say `Continue with`, the label says `or`, not `alternatively`.
Don't use it as a section heading. The label is small, muted text with no heading role; start a new section with a real heading.
Don't put it above the first or below the last block. It separates two blocks, so with only one side it points at nothing.

components.title: Skeleton
components.description: A pulsing placeholder shown while content is loading.

aria: Decorative: mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and announce the result, not the skeleton

parts.name: Skeleton
parts.description: A grey placeholder with a soft highlight that sweeps across it. `variant` picks the shape: `text` is a 14 px line, `title` a 20 px line two thirds wide, `avatar` a 40 px circle and `block` a 100 px box. It renders a plain `<div>` with no role and no label, and the highlight is not drawn under reduced motion.

items.text: Use a Skeleton while content with a known layout loads: a list, a card, a profile. For a short wait on an action, such as saving, use a Spinner.
Give each Skeleton the size of the content it stands for, using `variant` and a width class. The layout then keeps its height and does not jump when the content arrives.
Make a text placeholder as tall as the line it stands for. The `text` shape is 14 px high and a line of `text-sm` is 20 px, so add `my-0.75` (3 px) above and below it.
Draw what you already know, such as the table header or the card title, and put placeholders only where data is missing.

Set `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is loading and remove it when the content is in. Add a visually hidden `role="status"` line that says what is loading, because the placeholders themselves say nothing to screen readers.
Show a skeleton for the first load only. When data refreshes, keep the old content on screen and update it in place.
Don't fill the whole screen with blocks. Cover what is visible when the page opens and let the rest render with its data.
Don't leave a skeleton on screen when loading fails. Replace it with an error message and a way to try again.
Don't build your own placeholder for charts. They take a `loading` prop and draw a skeleton of the right height.

components.title: Tooltip
components.description: A short label shown on hover, in any of 4 directions.

props.name: onOpenChange

props.name: onOpenChangeComplete

props.name: open

props.name: trackCursorAxis

props.name: triggerId
props.description: ID of the trigger that the tooltip is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `open` prop to create a controlled tooltip. There's no need to specify this prop when the tooltip is uncontrolled (that is, when the `open` prop…

props.name: align
props.description: How to align the popup relative to the specified side.

props.name: anchor

props.description: Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against. May automatically change to avoid collisions.

props.name: sideOffset

props.description: Another tooltip will open instantly if the previous tooltip is closed within this timeout. Specified in milliseconds.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: How long to wait before closing the tooltip. Specified in milliseconds.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.description: Whether the tooltip should close when this trigger is clicked.

props.name: delay
props.description: How long to wait before opening the tooltip on hover. Specified in milliseconds.

props.name: disabled
props.description: If `true`, the tooltip will not open when interacting with this trigger. Note that this doesn't apply the `disabled` attribute to the trigger element. If you want to disable the trigger element itself, you can pass the `disabled` prop to t…

props.name: handle
props.description: A handle to associate the trigger with a tooltip.

props.name: payload
props.description: A payload to pass to the tooltip when it is opened.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

keyboard: Shown on keyboard focus as well as hover
Esc: dismiss
aria: Supplementary only: never the only label of a control (icon buttons need aria-label)
a11y.notes: Opens after 600 ms on hover by default (delay).

parts.name: Tooltip
parts.description: Holds the open state and links the trigger to the label. Control it with `open` and `onOpenChange`, switch it off with `disabled`, or leave it uncontrolled. Renders nothing itself.

parts.name: TooltipProvider
parts.description: Shares one delay between the tooltips below it, for example in a toolbar: the first opens after `delay` (600 ms by default), and moving to another trigger within `timeout` (300 ms) shows its tooltip at once. Without it, Base UI's own default delay applies.

parts.name: TooltipTrigger
parts.description: The element the tooltip describes. It opens on hover and on keyboard focus and points to the tooltip with `aria-describedby` while it is open. Pass your Button or IconButton through `render`; set `describe={false}` when the tooltip only repeats the trigger's own name.

parts.name: TooltipContent
parts.description: The dark surface, drawn in a portal on the `top` side by default, 8 px from the trigger. `side`, `align` and `sideOffset` move it, and it flips near a viewport edge. `maxWidth` wraps long text at 240 or 320 px. It has `role="tooltip"`; Escape closes it.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The text of the tooltip, the children of `TooltipContent`: one short phrase, 12 px medium, white.

parts.name: Shortcut
parts.description: A key hint in its own dark chip after the label, drawn from the `shortcut` prop. Write it for the platform: `⌘K` on macOS, `Ctrl+K` on Windows.

parts.name: Arrow
parts.description: The small point towards the trigger; `arrow={false}` hides it. It turns with the side the tooltip ends up on and keeps pointing at the middle of the trigger.

items.text: Use a Tooltip for a short hint on a control: the name of an icon button, a shortcut, a truncated text in full. For content people read at length or act on, use a Popover.

Give the trigger its own name with `aria-label`. The tooltip adds information and is never the only label of a control; set `describe={false}` when it repeats that name, so screen readers do not read it twice.
Keep the text to one short phrase without a full stop. Longer text wraps at 240 px, or 320 px with `maxWidth`; for more than three lines use a Popover.
Set `shortcut` only for a shortcut that works, written for the platform. Use `linger` for a confirmation such as `Copied to clipboard`, which then fades out slowly instead of snapping away.
Put the tooltips of a toolbar in one `TooltipProvider`, so the delay is the same everywhere and moving along the buttons shows each tooltip at once.
Make the reason a control is disabled visible without hover, for example as helper text. The tooltip, on a wrapper that can take focus, then only repeats it.
Place the tooltip where it covers neither a neighbouring control nor the text of the row. Choose `side` and `align` for that, and let it flip near the edge.
Don't put links or buttons in TooltipContent. It opens only on hover and focus of the trigger, so keyboard users cannot reach them.
Don't use a Tooltip as the only place for an error, a confirmation or task-critical information. Touch and keyboard users may never see it.
Don't put a tooltip on text that is not interactive. Nothing can take focus there, so a keyboard user never sees it.

components.title: Dialog
components.description: A modal window for focused tasks, built on Base UI.

props.name: handle

props.name: modal
props.description: Determines if the dialog enters a modal state when open. - `true`: user interaction is limited to just the dialog: focus is trapped, document page scroll is locked, and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled. - `false`: user…

props.name: onOpenChange

props.name: onOpenChangeComplete

props.name: open

props.name: triggerId
props.description: ID of the trigger that the dialog is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `open` prop to create a controlled dialog. There's no need to specify this prop when the dialog is uncontrolled (that is, when the `open` prop is…

props.name: scrollable

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: nativeButton

It brings its own portal and overlay and keeps focus inside while open. `size` is `sm` (384 px, default), `md` (512 px) or `lg` (720 px); `appearance` is `surface` (default: semibold title, footer band, shadow) or `plain` (the earlier flat look). `showOverlay={false}` with `modal={false}` on Dialog makes it non-modal, and `placement="bottom-right"` anchors it to the corner.

parts.name: DialogIcon

parts.name: DialogDescription

parts.name: DialogBody
parts.description: The slot between header and footer for a form, a list or text. With `scrollable` the body scrolls between two rules while title and footer stay in place; it is focusable so keyboard users can scroll.

parts.name: DialogFooter
parts.description: The row of buttons. The last button in the markup sits on the right, and on top on a phone. `band` paints the full-width footer fill, `layout` is `inline` or `stacked` (primary on top, full-width buttons), `start` puts one action at the left edge (Back, Compare).

parts.name: DialogClose

parts.name: Action
parts.description: The primary Button, last in the footer. Name it after its result, such as Send invite, and show its pending state while the request runs.

parts.name: DialogOverlay

parts.name: DialogPortal

items.text: Always include a `DialogTitle`, also when the design shows none. Without it the dialog has no name for screen readers.
Put the main action last in `DialogFooter` and name it after its result: `Send invite`, `Create project`, not `OK`. Keep Cancel neutral next to it.
On a failed submit keep the dialog open, keep the input and put the message on the field or in an Alert at the top of the body.
While the request runs, show the pending state on the primary action and disable the others. Close the dialog only after the server confirmed.
Put long content in `DialogBody scrollable` so the title and the footer stay in view.
Don't confirm a destructive action in a Dialog: a click outside closes it. An Alert Dialog closes only through a button or Escape.
Don't use a dialog to report that something worked. A saved state is a toast; a dialog that needs one click to dismiss only adds a step.
Don't discard unsaved input silently when the dialog closes. Ask with an Alert Dialog on top: Keep editing returns to the form.
Don't nest dialogs or use a dialog for a long flow. More than four steps belong on a page.
