topics.summary: Re-theme by overriding tokens: brand colour, dark mode, a themed subtree, density.
topics.body:
Every colour, radius and motion value in WunderUI is a CSS variable. A theme is a set of token overrides, never restyled components. - **Where tokens live.** Light values on `:root`, dark values on `.dark` — the same names in both (`wunderui-cli docs tokens` lists them). Import your theme file after `@wunderui/react/styles.css`, so your values win. - **Brand colour.** `--primary` points at the brand scale (`var(--brand-600)`), an eleven-step scale from `--brand-50` to `--brand-1000`. Replace the scale and the brand tokens follow: primary, `--ring`, `--text-link`, `--chart-1`. Pick the steps so text keeps WCAG AA contrast in light and dark. - **Generate it.** The free agent skill `wunderui-theme` builds the scale from one hex colour, checks contrast and writes one CSS file. The Theme Builder (https://wunderui.com/theme-builder) does the same in the browser. - **Dark mode** is the `.dark` class on ``. `ThemeProvider` (from `@wunderui/react`, built on next-themes) sets it and remembers the choice; never write your own dark colours. - **Radius and fonts** are tokens too (`--radius`, the font variables): override them in the same file. - **Only part of a page** can carry another theme: set the variables on a wrapper element, everything inside follows. ## Re-theming a subtree ```tsx
{/* every WunderUI component inside now uses the new accent */}
``` ## Density Compact is the default: controls are 32, 36, 40, 44 and 48 px (`sm` to `2xl`), one scale for buttons and fields, text stays 14 px. `data-density="comfortable"` on `` or any ancestor restores the roomier sizes (36 to 56 px); it nests in both directions. In code: ``, `DensityProvider` and `useDensity()`. Do not hard-code control heights (`h-9`, `h-11`) — use the component sizes so density keeps working. Portals (menus, dialogs) read the page's density.

topics.title: Spacing
topics.summary: One spacing system for dashboards, templates and form cards: page padding, section and card gaps, card padding.
topics.body:
## Spacing

One spacing system for dashboards, templates and blocks, on a 4-px base. Use only these steps:
2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48. The gap inside a group is smaller than the gap between groups.
Desktop means `lg` (1024 px) and up; card padding switches at `md` (768 px).

| Area | Desktop | Mobile | Tailwind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top bar | none, the page header sits in the content | 56, padding 12 / 12 / 12 / 16, bottom border | `h-14` |
| Page padding left and right | 32 | 16 | `px-4 lg:px-8` |
| Page padding top / bottom | 32 / 48 | 32 / 48 | `pt-8 pb-12` |
| Page title → supporting text | 2 | 2 | `gap-0.5` |
| Title block → tabs or filters (tabs start the next section) | 32 | 32 | `gap-8` |
| Tabs or filters → their content (same section) | 16 | 16 | `gap-4` |
| Buttons in an action row | 8 | 8 | `gap-2` |
| Gap between sections | 32 | 32 | `gap-8` |
| Section header → content | 16 (header: 16 bottom padding, bottom border) | 16 | `gap-4`, `pb-4 border-b` |
| Card gap | 24 | 20 | `gap-5 lg:gap-6` |
| Cards in a KPI row | 16 | 16 | `gap-4` |
| Main column ↔ right rail (a card gap) | 24 | 24, stacked | `gap-6` |
| Card padding (every card) | 16 | 16 | `p-4` |
| Card inner gap | 16 | 16 | `gap-4` |
| Card radius | 16 | 16 | `rounded-xl` |
| KPI label → value → trend | 8 → 8 | 8 → 8 | `gap-2` |
| Tables | in their card | full bleed, no radius | `-mx-4 rounded-none lg:mx-0 lg:rounded-xl` |

Three card types: modal card (sign-in, sign-up, verification; stands alone on a screen or in a modal) with padding 48 top and bottom and 40 left and right; standard card (KPI, chart, widget and everything else) with padding 16 and inner gap 16; table / list card with padding 16, List Panel rows 8 px from the card edge. Auth card gaps: title → subtitle 8, header → first
field 24, label → input 8, input → helper 4, field → field 20, last field → primary button 24,
button → divider → alternatives 24 and 24, stacked buttons 8.

topics.title: Motion
topics.summary: Duration, easing and travel tokens, the motion rules and ready recipes.
topics.body:
Motion is tokenised like everything else. Duration and easing are never written as raw values — a hand-typed `300ms` with `ease-in-out` is the default every generator produces, and it is why generated interfaces feel generic. ### Duration Tailwind v4 has no `--duration-*` theme namespace, so WunderUI ships the scale as named utilities defined with `@utility`. Each one sets `--tw-duration` as well, which is what `tw-animate-css` reads — so `data-open:duration-base` works on an `animate-in` the same way it works on a `transition`. | Token | Value | Reach for it when | | --- | --- | --- | | `duration-instant` | `80ms` | Tooltip dismiss, press release. Barely reads as motion. | | `duration-fast` | `150ms` | The default exit. Hover, focus ring, checkbox, switch track. | | `duration-base` | `250ms` | Dropdown, popover, context menu, backdrop, collapse. | | `duration-slow` | `350ms` | Dialog, toast, switch thumb — a surface arriving. | | `duration-deliberate` | `450ms` | A side panel and a full-width panel. Rare. | | `duration-ambient` | `700ms` | Progress and meter fills. Data moving, not chrome. | ### Easing `ease-*` is a Tailwind v4 namespace, so these are utilities: `ease-entrance`, `ease-exit`, `ease-move`, `ease-overshoot`. | Utility | Curve | Reach for it when | | --- | --- | --- | | `ease-entrance` | `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` | Anything arriving. Fast start, long settle. The house curve. | | `ease-exit` | `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)` | Anything leaving. Accelerates away. | | `ease-move` | `cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)` | Anything repositioning while staying on screen. | | `ease-overshoot` | `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.35, 0.64, 1)` | Dialog, popover, switch. At most one per screen. | | `ease-spring` | `linear(0, 0.35 9%, 0.78 19%, 1.04 27%, 1.1 32%, 1.03 41%, 0.98 50%, 1.01 62%, 1)` | A sampled spring: one soft overshoot, then it settles. Something physical landing — a thumb, an arrow, a released sheet. Never on a data value. | ### Travel | Token | Value | Reach for it when | | --- | --- | --- | | `--travel-xs` | `2px` | Tooltip — stays glued to its anchor. | | `--travel-sm` | `4px` | Popover, dropdown, context menu. | | `--travel-md` | `8px` | Dialog, toast, inline panel. | | `--travel-lg` | `16px` | Section reveal on scroll. | | `--scale-press` | `0.97` | Pressed button. | | `--scale-enter` | `0.96` | Dialog arriving. | ### Rules 1. **Duration and easing are class names, not numbers.** `duration-base`, `ease-entrance`. Tailwind has no `--duration-*` theme namespace, so WunderUI ships these as `@utility` rules that also set `--tw-duration` — which means they work on `animate-in` / `animate-out` too. 2. **Only `transform` and `opacity`.** Everything else goes through layout or paint. Height animates via `grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr`, never via `height`. 3. **Entrances decelerate, exits accelerate.** `ease-entrance` in, `ease-exit` out — and the exit is one step shorter on the duration scale, never the entrance duration reversed. 4. **Never fade in the LCP element.** An element at `opacity: 0` is not an LCP candidate, so a 600ms hero fade adds 600ms to your LCP. Render headline copy at full opacity; animate `transform` only. 5. **Restrain the travel.** Anything anchored to a trigger moves `--travel-xs` or `--travel-sm`. A menu that slides 20px looks like it fell in. 6. **One overshoot per screen.** `ease-overshoot` is punctuation. Two of them on one view and the interface reads as a toy. Never on a data value: a bar, gauge or bubble that swings past its number shows a wrong number for a moment. 7. **Reduced motion is opt-in, not a kill switch.** Wrap the animation in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` so the still state is the default and you cannot forget a selector. Reduced means calmer, not nothing: drop transforms and travel, keep opacity and colour changes (rule 15). 8. **Never `transition-all`.** Name the properties — `transition-[opacity,transform]` — or use bare `transition`, which covers colour, shadow, transform and opacity but no layout property. `transition-all` animates things you did not mean to animate, including on first paint. 9. **Loading keeps its height.** A skeleton occupies the same box as the content it stands in for, and crossfades — it never collapses and reflows. 10. **A looping ambient animation is the one place `ease-in-out` belongs.** A shimmer that runs forever has no entrance and no exit, so symmetry is correct there and nowhere else. 11. **Animate by frequency.** Keyboard-driven and 100+/day actions (command palette, shortcuts, moving between tooltips) get no motion; tens a day get a short fade; rare moments may delight. Tooltips skip their entrance when another one was just open (`data-open:data-instant:animate-none`). 12. **Anchored surfaces grow from their trigger.** Popover, dropdown, tooltip, hover card and select use `origin-(--transform-origin)`. Never start from `scale(0)` — start at 0.92–0.97 with opacity. Centred dialogs are exempt. 13. **Toggles stay interruptible.** Animate switches, checkboxes, tabs and other repeated state changes with transitions — they retarget from wherever they are — never with keyframes bound to the state, which restart from zero. An overshoot transition (`transition-transform duration-base ease-overshoot`) still swings past the end. 14. **Hover only where hover exists.** Tailwind v4's `hover:` is already gated to `(hover: hover)`; hand-written `:hover` in CSS goes inside `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`, so a tap on a phone does not leave a hover state stuck. 15. **Reduced motion keeps the fade.** WunderUI's global rule zeroes the scale, slide, spin and blur of every `animate-in` / `animate-out` and every transform transition, and keeps opacity and colour — so do not add `motion-reduce:transition-none` or `motion-reduce:animate-none` to a fade. ### Motion recipes #### Overlay enter and exit ```tsx /* Dialog, sheet, popover, dropdown, context menu — one pattern for all of them. Base UI exposes data-open / data-closed; tw-animate-css turns them into keyframes. */ ``` #### Collapse without a fixed height ```tsx
{children}
``` #### Press feedback ```tsx

topics.title: Accessibility
topics.summary: Labels, focus, keyboard, contrast, reduced motion and announcements with WunderUI.
topics.body:
WunderUI's interactive components are built on Base UI primitives, which bring the roles, focus handling and keyboard behaviour of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices. Most accessibility bugs come from what is put around them. `wunderui-cli component <name>` shows the keys and ARIA of one component.

## Names and labels

- Every form control has a visible label: `Field` with `Label`, or `Label` around the control. A placeholder is not a name.
- Icon-only buttons (`IconButton`, an icon `Toggle`) need `aria-label`. A `Tooltip` is supplementary and never the only name.
- Dialogs get a `DialogTitle` (their accessible name) and usually a `DialogDescription`.
- Sliders, meters and progress bars need a label when the text around them does not name them.

## Keyboard and focus

- Keep the primitives: to change the rendered element use the `render` prop instead of wrapping the component in a clickable `div`.
- Never remove the focus ring. It uses the `--ring` token, so a theme can recolour it but should not hide it.
- Order the DOM the way the screen reads. Do not use positive `tabIndex`.
- Touch targets are at least 40 px; the compact control sizes keep the hit area.

## Colour and contrast

- Text tokens on their intended surfaces meet WCAG AA in light and dark. Hard-coded colours do not get that guarantee — use the token utilities.
- A custom brand colour has to pass AA as well: the `wunderui-theme` skill checks every key pair and moves shades until they pass.
- Never use colour alone for meaning: a status badge also has a word or an icon.

## Motion

- Wrap custom animation in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. Reduced motion keeps fades and drops movement (`wunderui-cli docs motion`, rules 7 and 15).
- Nothing used from the keyboard or many times a day animates.

## Announcements

- A message that appears after an action goes into a `Toast` (announced through its live region) or an `aria-live="polite"` region — an `Alert` that is simply rendered is not announced.
- Loading regions: `aria-busy="true"` while loading, then announce the result, not the skeleton.

## Check

- `wunderui-cli doctor` checks the project setup; the `wunderui-a11y` skill (Pro) renders every variant, walks the focus order and measures contrast.

topics.title: Copy
topics.summary: Rules for the words in the product: buttons, errors, empty states, numbers.
topics.body:
Rules for the words inside the product — buttons, labels, errors and empty states.

1. **Buttons say what happens.** A verb and, where it helps, the object: `Save changes`, `Invite member`, `Delete project` — never `OK`, `Submit` or `Yes`. The destructive button repeats the action, the other one is `Cancel`.
2. **Sentence case everywhere in the product.** Buttons, menu items, headings, labels and tabs start with one capital: `Billing history`, not `Billing History`.
3. **Errors say what happened and what to do.** `The card was declined. Try another card or contact your bank.` — no `Oops`, no `Something went wrong` on its own, no blame, no error codes without words.
4. **Empty states explain and offer one action.** What will appear here, why it is empty, and the one button that fills it: `No invoices yet — your first one appears after the first payment.`
5. **Labels are nouns, hints are sentences.** A field label names the thing (`Work email`); help text under it explains a rule in a full sentence.
6. **Numbers carry their unit.** Money with the ISO currency or symbol and two decimals (`$299.00`, `EUR 41.80`), percentages with `%`, durations and sizes with units (`12 GB`, `3 min`). Use tabular numbers in tables.
7. **No filler.** No `please`, `simply`, `just` or `easily`; no exclamation marks in the interface; no `Lorem ipsum`. Sample people are invented (`Alina Lorenz`, `Felix Brandt`).
8. **Confirmations name the object.** `Delete “Q4 report”?` with what is lost, not `Are you sure?`.

topics.title: Agent skills
topics.summary: The agent skills that build and check with these rules.
topics.body:
Agent skills that build and check with these rules (https://wunderui.com/skills):

- **wunderui-screen** (Free) — Builds a complete React screen with WunderUI from a one-sentence request, within the user's plan (Free uses only the free components) — picks the components and a matching block layout, fills props from design.json, adds the empty, loading and error states that generated screens usually forget, uses motion tokens instead of raw milliseconds, and finishes with a typecheck and a build.
- **wunderui-setup** (Free) — Sets up WunderUI in a React project from scratch to the first rendered screen — detects the framework, Tailwind version and existing tokens, puts DESIGN.md and design.json into the project, registers the WunderUI MCP server, wires styles.css and the @source path, renders a probe component and writes a setup report.
- **wunderui-theme** (Free) — Generates a complete WunderUI brand theme from one brand colour (hex) — optionally an accent colour, a radius preference and a font — the eleven-step brand scale (--brand-50 … --brand-1000), the brand tokens derived from it (primary, primary-foreground, text-link, ring, tint and tint text, chart 1) for light and dark, a WCAG AA check of every key pair with shades moved automatically until they pass, and one CSS file to import after @wunderui/react/styles.css (globally or for one subtree), plus a report.
- **wunderui-token-check** (Free) — Finds hard-coded colours, spacing and radii that bypass the WunderUI design tokens, maps each literal to the nearest token with a measured distance (ΔE for colour, px for spacing and radius), separates safe swaps from values too far from any token, replaces the safe ones and reports how much the look changed.
- **wunderui-a11y** (Pro) — Accessibility check per component or screen in a WunderUI project — renders every variant, walks the focus order and checks that focus is visible, measures WCAG AA contrast of every text in light and dark, verifies the reduced-motion fallback, and delivers each finding with a patch instead of just a report.
- **wunderui-compose** (Pro) — Composes WunderUI blocks into a complete page — clarifies the page's goal and audience, proposes a block order that follows the visitor's questions, inserts the blocks and fills them with real content, checks the rhythm (one notable effect per section) and protects the LCP element from entrance animation.
- **wunderui-figma-screen** (Pro) — Builds a screen in Figma from the WunderUI library — real component instances instead of drawn rectangles, every fill and text bound to the theme variables and text styles, auto layout throughout, a light frame first, then the dark frame as a clone with the Dark mode and a 390 px mobile frame — and checks the result with screenshots and an audit (unbound paints, unstyled text, absolute children).
- **wunderui-figma-sync** (Pro) — Keeps Figma variables and the project's CSS tokens (styles.css) identical in both directions — reads the Figma variable collections and text styles through the Figma MCP server, diffs them against the CSS custom properties (colour per light/dark mode, spacing, radius, type, motion), lists every conflict with the measured difference, asks which side wins and writes only in that direction, then reports what changed.
- **wunderui-motion-audit** (Pro) — Audits a codebase's animations and transitions against the WunderUI motion rules — transition-all, raw millisecond durations, ease-in-out and other generic curves, scroll-driven animations without an @supports fallback, missing prefers-reduced-motion handling, layout-property animation and fades on the LCP element — justifies every finding with the rule from DESIGN.md, proposes and applies a patch with motion tokens and verifies the build.
- **wunderui-refactor** (Pro) — Migrates an existing React app to WunderUI — scans the project and detects the UI stack per file (shadcn/ui, Radix primitives, MUI, Chakra, Headless UI, Mantine, hand-built components and hard-coded Tailwind colours), maps every component to its WunderUI equivalent with prop notes, writes a migration plan with effort and order, applies the safe codemods (shadcn imports → @wunderui/react, raw colours → token utilities) and measures before → after (raw colours, foreign UI imports, WunderUI coverage) with the project's typecheck.
- **wunderui-uiux-design-auditor** (Pro) — Evidence-based UI/UX and accessibility audit of any product — live websites, landing pages, component libraries / front-end code (React, Vue, Svelte, HTML/CSS, Tailwind) and Figma files — against a 520-rule catalog (WCAG 2.2 A/AA, platform guidance, design-system rules, responsive behaviour from 320 to 1440 px).

playbooks.title: Agent run view
playbooks.summary: Show what an AI agent is doing: status, steps, tool calls, approvals, cost and failure — every state including abort.
playbooks.layout: One column (max-w-3xl): status line on top, the steps below, pending decisions in a highlighted Card.

steps.title: Status
steps.do: A Badge with the run state (running, waiting, done, failed) and the elapsed time next to the title.

steps.title: Steps
steps.do: Timeline with one item per step (title, tool, duration) and a Progress for steps done of planned. The free plan has no agent components: name them as the upgrade.

steps.title: Approval
steps.do: A Card that states the action, its risk and what changes, with Approve and Reject Buttons; destructive approvals confirm in an AlertDialog.

steps.title: Cost
steps.do: A Meter with spend against the budget and the numbers next to it.

steps.title: Failure
steps.do: An Alert (negative) with the failed step, the reason and Retry / Resume Buttons.

states: queued and running: the status says so; streaming steps append without moving what is already there
waiting for approval: the decision is the most visible element; nothing else asks for attention
failed: the failed step is marked and the error says what to do next
aborted by the user: a calm final state with what was done and what was not
empty: no runs yet → EmptyState with how to start one

tokens: States through Badge tints and the status tokens, not ad-hoc colours
motion: Streaming text and steps appear without layout jumps
No looping animation except an ambient shimmer on the running state
a11y: Approve and reject are buttons with their action in the label
The run can be stopped with the keyboard
copy: Steps in plain words ("Read 3 files"); tool names in code style only where they help

checks: Play every state: running, waiting, failed, aborted, done

paid.note: Core and Pro add more components and ready-made blocks for this screen (https://wunderui.com/#pricing).

playbooks.title: Dashboard
playbooks.summary: An overview screen: KPI row, trends, a table of recent records and activity — every region with loading, empty and error.
playbooks.layout: A container (mx-auto max-w-6xl p-6); a KPI row (grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-4), then main + side (grid gap-6 xl:grid-cols-[minmax(0,2fr)_minmax(0,1fr)]).

steps.title: Frame
steps.do: A page container with the title row; sections of a bigger product go into Tabs.

steps.title: Header
steps.do: An h1, a one-line description and a row with the date range control and the one primary action.

steps.title: KPI row
steps.do: One Card per KPI with number value and a TrendChip; a Meter or Progress when the KPI has a target.

steps.title: Trends
steps.do: The free plan has no charts: show the period numbers in a Widget with number value, TrendChip and Meter bars, and say that charts come with Core and Pro. Never draw a chart by hand.

steps.title: Records
steps.do: Table with header, rows and a footer link to the full list; Pagination when it pages.

steps.title: Activity
steps.do: A Timeline of recent events in the side column, newest first, five to eight items.

states: loading: charts take loading; KPI cards and tables get Skeleton blocks of the same height — the layout must not jump
empty: no data yet → EmptyState with what will appear and the action that fills it ("Connect a data source")
error: per region — Alert (negative) with what failed and a Retry button; the other regions keep working
edge: 0, negative and very large numbers format correctly; long names truncate inside their cell

tokens: Numbers in tabular-nums; chart colours only from --chart-1 … --chart-5
Status colours through Badge and TrendChip, not hand-picked hex
motion: Charts animate themselves; never an overshoot on a data value (motion rule 6)
No entrance animation on every page load; at most a short stagger the first time
a11y: Trends carry a sign and a word, not only colour
Every KPI has a visible label; the page has one h1
copy: Empty states explain and offer one action

checks: Look at loading, empty and error of each region in light and dark, and at 390 px

paid.note: Core and Pro add more components and ready-made blocks for this screen (https://wunderui.com/#pricing).

playbooks.title: Form page
playbooks.summary: Create or edit a record: grouped fields, the right control per value, validation that helps, one clear submit.
playbooks.layout: One column (max-w-xl) on the page, or a Dialog / sheet for five fields or fewer. Fieldsets group related fields; the actions sit at the end, primary first in reading order.

steps.title: Groups
steps.do: Fieldset with a legend per group (Details, Address, Billing); three to seven fields per group.

steps.title: Stages
steps.do: For a long form, split it into sections with headings and a Progress showing how far along the user is.

steps.title: Fields
steps.do: Field + label per value, with the control that fits: Input / Textarea for text, NumberField for numbers, DatePicker for dates, RadioGroup for one of few, InlineSelect or Combobox for one of many, Checkbox for consent, DropZone for files.

steps.title: Actions
steps.do: A row at the end: the primary submit ("Create project") and a plain Cancel Button.

steps.title: Result
steps.do: On success, a toast names what was created and the page moves on; on a server error, an Alert above the form says what failed and keeps every value.

states: submitting: the submit Button shows a Spinner, keeps its width and cannot be pressed twice
invalid: validate on submit, then live per field; FieldError under the field, focus on the first invalid field
server error: Alert (negative) above the form, values kept
edit mode: Skeleton fields while the record loads; Save changes is disabled until something changed

tokens: Controls use the size scale (sm … 2xl), never fixed heights like h-11
Error text via FieldError, not a hand-picked red
motion: No motion on validation messages beyond the components' own
a11y: Every control has a visible label; required fields are marked in the label, not only with colour
Errors are tied to their field (Field does it) and the first one gets focus on submit
autocomplete attributes for names, emails, addresses and one-time codes
copy: Labels are nouns ("Work email"), hints are sentences
The submit button says what happens ("Create project", "Send message")

playbooks.summary: Sign in (and sign up) on a centred card: email and password or a provider, errors that help, a code step for 2FA.

steps.title: Card
steps.do: One Card with the product logo, a title ("Sign in to Acme") and one sentence below it.

states: submitting: the button shows a Spinner and keeps its width; fields stay filled
error: wrong credentials → Alert (negative) above the form that does not say which field was wrong; field-level problems (empty, not an email) → FieldError
locked or expired: a dedicated message with the way out (reset link, contact)
success: go straight to the app; no success screen

tokens: Page bg-page, card bg-card; the primary button is the only primary element
motion: No entrance animation on the card or the headline (it is the LCP element)
Errors appear without shaking the form
a11y: Labels are visible; never placeholder-only fields
autocomplete attributes on email, password and one-time-code; paste stays allowed
After a failed submit, move focus to the error summary or the first invalid field

playbooks.title: Settings page
playbooks.summary: Account, profile and workspace settings: grouped forms, toggles, a danger zone, saved with feedback.
playbooks.layout: A centred column (mx-auto max-w-3xl p-6) with the title on top and Tabs for the sections; every section is a Card. Below sm the tab list scrolls sideways.

steps.title: Frame
steps.do: A centred container (mx-auto max-w-3xl p-6) with a Breadcrumb above the title.

steps.title: Header
steps.do: An h1 and one sentence on what the page controls. No primary button here: saving happens per section.

steps.title: Sections
steps.do: Tabs for the groups (Profile, Notifications, Security, Billing). Inside a tab, one Card per group of settings with a title and a short description.

steps.title: Fields
steps.do: Field with a label, the control and a description where a rule needs explaining. Switch for on/off preferences, RadioGroup for one of a few, InlineSelect for one of many.

steps.title: Rows
steps.do: Lay each Field out in two columns from sm (label and description left, control right) so the controls align.

steps.title: Save
steps.do: A Save changes button in each Card footer, disabled until something changed; Cancel resets the section. After saving, a toast confirms it.

steps.title: Danger zone
steps.do: A separate Card at the end. The destructive button opens an AlertDialog that names the object and what is lost ("Delete workspace Acme?").

states: loading: Skeleton in the shape of each Card (same height and radius) while the settings load
saving: the Save button shows a Spinner and keeps its width; the fields stay editable
empty: a section without entries yet (API keys, sessions) gets an EmptyState with one action
error: loading failed → Alert (negative) with a Retry button in place of the Card; saving failed → keep the input, show FieldError or a toast that says what failed

tokens: Cards bg-card on bg-page, borders border-border, text text-foreground / text-text-secondary — no hex
gap-6 between Cards; the components bring their own padding
motion: No entrance animation for the page; Switch, Tabs, toasts and AlertDialog animate themselves — add nothing
Custom transitions only with duration-* and ease-* tokens, never transition-all
a11y: Every control has a visible label (Field / Label); Switch labels say what is on ("Email me weekly reports")
Destructive actions confirm in an AlertDialog; focus returns to the trigger
Validation errors sit next to the field (FieldError) and are tied to it
copy: Buttons say what happens: Save changes, Delete workspace
Sentence case for tabs, titles and labels

checks: Look at every state (e.g. ?state=loading|empty|error) in light and dark, and at 390 px

playbooks.title: Table page
playbooks.summary: A list of records: search, filters, sorting, row actions, bulk actions and a detail panel, with every empty case.
playbooks.layout: Container (mx-auto max-w-6xl p-6): title row with the primary action, a toolbar row, then the table full width. On mobile the table scrolls inside its own container.

steps.title: Header
steps.do: Title, record count and the one primary action ("New invoice").

steps.title: Toolbar
steps.do: InputGroup with a search icon and Input; filters in a Popover with Checkbox lists or a Combobox; active filters as Badges with a clear action.

steps.title: Table
steps.do: Table with a caption, header, rows and typed cells (UserCell, BadgeCell, CurrencyCell); Pagination below. Sorting state lives in the URL.

steps.title: Row actions
steps.do: An IconButton with aria-label at the end of each row that opens a Popover with the actions.

steps.title: Bulk actions
steps.do: Row checkboxes; when rows are selected, ActionBar shows the count and the bulk actions. Destructive bulk actions confirm in an AlertDialog.

states: loading: Skeleton rows with the table's row height; the header stays
empty (nothing created yet): EmptyState with what the list holds and the create action
empty (filters match nothing): say so and offer "Clear filters" — a different message from the first-run empty state
error: Alert (negative) above the table with Retry; keep filters and search
edge: long names truncate in their cell with the full value in the detail; 0 and very large amounts format correctly

tokens: Amounts and dates in tabular-nums, amounts right-aligned
Status as Badge with a tint, never coloured text alone
motion: No row animations on sort or filter; sheet and dialogs bring their own motion
a11y: The table has a caption (visible or sr-only); sortable headers expose aria-sort
Row checkboxes are labelled ("Select invoice INV-104"); icon buttons have aria-label
The table scrolls inside its container, never the page
copy: Column titles are nouns in sentence case
Bulk actions name the count: "Delete 3 invoices"

checks: Try 0, 1 and 500 rows, a filter with no match, and a failed load

Use when the user asks for a page, screen, view, dashboard, settings page, table view, form or similar in a project that uses WunderUI (@wunderui/react).

skills.name: wunderui-setup

Use when the user wants to install, add, set up or connect WunderUI (or "@wunderui/react") in a project, or asks why WunderUI components render unstyled.

skills.name: wunderui-theme

skills.name: wunderui-token-check

Use when the user asks to check or clean up tokens, remove hardcoded colours/hex values, make a codebase use the design system, or before a theming or dark-mode change in a WunderUI project.
